columns.rationale: null_rate is 0.0 with distinct_count 16 equal to the row_count of 16, and distinct_values show short IATA-style codes (e.g. 9E, AA, DL, UA), so carrier is a fully populated, apparently unique identifier.

null_rate is 0.0 with 16 distinct values that are full airline company names (e.g. 'Delta Air Lines Inc.', 'Southwest Airlines Co.'); renamed from the generic 'name' to 'airline_name' for clarity since it describes the carrier, not a person or other entity.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata true; this is a capture-tool surrogate id with no business meaning, dropped per convention.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata true with a single constant value '2026-09-02T23:26:17' across all 16 rows, confirming it is a load-time stamp rather than business data; dropped per convention.
Flagged is_airbyte_metadata true with the single distinct value '{}' across all rows, carrying no usable information; dropped per convention.

decisions.rationale: carrier has distinct_count 16 exactly matching dataset.row_count of 16 with null_rate 0.0, making it the smallest column set that plausibly identifies one row.
dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 against a row_count of 16, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is required.

_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are each marked is_airbyte_metadata true in the profile and carry only capture-tool bookkeeping (a surrogate id, a constant extraction timestamp, and an empty JSON object), so they are dropped.

The bronze column 'name' holds full airline company names (16 distinct values, null_rate 0.0) and is renamed to 'airline_name' in silver so consumers do not mistake it for a person or generic entity name.

purpose: This table is a small reference dataset mapping airline carrier codes to their full airline company names, intended to feed carrier/airline dimension lookups in downstream analytics on NYC flight data.
usage: Join other flight fact tables to this table on the carrier code to resolve the human-readable airline_name for display or grouping; both columns are fully populated (null_rate 0.0) so no null-handling logic is required by consumers.
limitations: The table is tiny (row_count 16) and duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 so no deduplication logic was needed; uniqueness of carrier as a grain key is inferred from distinct_count matching row_count rather than from an explicit profiled constraint, so a human should confirm this against the full warehouse history before relying on it as a primary key.
